title: implementation-plan
description: Structured implementation plan for a regulatory change, supervisory finding, or enforcement remediation. Workstreams, milestones, owners by role, dependencies, acceptance criteria, governance cadence, implementation risks, resource asks, and BAU handoff. Sized for a regulatory-change PMO and a steering or executive committee. Chains upstream from rule-to-obligation-extraction, policy-diff, and any control-gap output; chains downstream into BAU obligation inventory and ongoing monitoring.

plan_id.description: Stable ID for the plan. Reused across all artifacts produced during the implementation programme.

engagement_id.description: Optional pointer to the scope record under which this plan was produced.

as_of_date.description: Date the plan was last revised.

trigger.description: What initiated the plan. The plan inherits its evidence posture from the trigger.

source_citation.description: Named, dated source for the trigger (e.g., 'CFPB final rule, 12 CFR Part 1002 Subpart B, Section 1071, March 2023').

trigger_id.description: Internal ID for the trigger (e.g., MRA number, consent-order docket, issue-management ID).

effective_date.description: Mandatory compliance date. For tiered rules, the tier applicable to this institution; tier-specific dates are captured per workstream where they vary.

tiered_compliance_dates.description: Where the rule has tiered compliance dates and the institution touches more than one tier. Each entry pairs a population (e.g., loans originated above a threshold) with its applicable date.

obligations_in_scope.description: Obligation IDs from rule-to-obligation-extraction or the firm's obligation inventory.

gaps_in_scope.description: Finding IDs from policy-diff and any control-gap input.

scope_and_source_posture.description: Scope confirmation in writing. The shape mirrors the scope record.

workstreams.description: Workstream breakdown. Each workstream covers a coherent set of obligations and gaps with a single owner role and an explicit milestone chain.

name.description: Plain-language workstream name (e.g., 'Origination platform changes', 'Firewall design', 'Reporting build').

owner_role.description: Workstream owner role. Roles only, never named individuals.

second_line_oversight_role.description: Second-line role accountable for control-design review and challenge.

items.description: Workstream IDs this workstream depends on.

owner_role.description: Milestone owner role if different from the workstream owner.

items.description: Other milestone IDs this milestone depends on.

acceptance_criteria.description: Evidence-based criteria. Each criterion describes the artifact that demonstrates closure, not the activity.

items.description: Artifact pointer the milestone produces (system-of-record path, document name, dataset reference).

second_line_review_required.description: True when second-line confirmation of control design is required before the milestone closes.

governance_checkpoints.description: Committees and cadences that govern the programme. Steering, executive, and board cadences as warranted by criticality.

body.description: Committee or forum (e.g., regulatory change steering committee, executive risk committee, board risk committee, audit committee).

decision_rights.description: What decisions this body owns (e.g., scope changes above $X, milestone slippage acceptance, resource ask approval).

escalation_trigger.description: What triggers an out-of-cycle escalation (e.g., milestone slippage past T+30, identified control gap with customer impact, regulator follow-up question).

reporting_artifact.description: What artifact the body consumes (RAG status pack, milestone tracker, risk register).

implementation_risks.description: Implementation risk register. Delivery risks plus second-order risks (control drift during change, key-person, vendor delivery, data-readiness).

early_warning_indicator.description: Observable signal that the risk is materialising.

resource_asks.description: Explicit named asks. Generic 'more resources' requests do not survive a steering committee.

role.description: Role being asked for (e.g., business analyst with 1071 LOS experience; QA tester for firewall verification).

budget_amount.description: Budget amount with currency (e.g., 'USD 250k for Q3-Q4 vendor work').

justification.description: Why the ask is needed and what milestones it unblocks.

if_declined.description: Consequence if the ask is declined: which milestone slips, by how long, with what residual risk.

regulator_readiness_checkpoints.description: Pre-effective-date checkpoints that demonstrate readiness ahead of supervision. Mock submissions, dry-run tests, attestations, regulator office-hours engagement.

evidence_produced.description: Artifact the checkpoint produces (mock submission file, attestation memo, control-test workpaper).

effective_date_posture.description: Adoption posture relative to the mandatory date. Early adoption is a posture choice with implications; late adoption is a risk choice with implications.

contingency_plan.description: What the firm does if a milestone slips past the mandatory date. Manual workaround, scope reduction, regulator engagement.

open_questions.description: Open questions for legal, business, regulatory liaison. Each question names the audience and the decision the answer unlocks.

handoff_to_bau.description: Transition into business-as-usual. The remediation closes; the obligation lands in the obligation inventory with an ongoing monitoring cadence.

target_owner_role.description: Role that owns the obligation in BAU.

monitoring_cadence.description: Ongoing monitoring frequency (e.g., quarterly control test, annual attestation, monthly KRI review).

obligation_inventory_pointer.description: Where the obligation is recorded in the firm's obligation inventory.

review_gates.description: Named human-review gates this plan must clear before sign-off, per references/review-gates.md.

source_trace.description: Citations supporting material claims about the rule, supervisory expectations, transition mechanics, and remediation conventions.
